items.summary: Detecting Design and Architecture Smells with LLM-Based and Agentic Strategies This repository contains the replication package for the study: How Context Shapes LLM-Based and Agentic Detection of Design and Architecture Smells The study evaluates how different context construction strategies affect the detection of design and architecture smells using Large Language Models (LLMs) and coding agents. We compare direct LLM invocation with predefined contexts against Mini-swe-agent-based repository exploration. items.summary: On a supplied real Euclidean two-plane, admitting both rotations and reflections gives the transport group O(2) = U(1) ⋊ Z₂, not an untwisted circle. We organize the resulting graph, face, refinement, and readout structures in one assumption-controlled framework. On a connected finite graph, tree gauge reduces the edge data to a simultaneous conjugacy class of free generators. Its determinant class lies in H¹(Γ; Z₂), while the phase is a crossed cocycle for the associated sign action. Admitting faces introduces additional path comparisons: their determinant defects obey a relative boundary law, and a rooted tetrahedral word gives an exact non-Abelian Bianchi identity whose phase sum is sign-twisted. Shared-edge and common-root data permit exact boundary cancellation under the stated disk refinements. Explicit pentagonal and hexagonal certificates include all five and fourteen triangulations, respectively, and two mixed 1–3, 2–2, 3–1 routes. Mismatched-edge and omitted-root controls distinguish invalid fusion, while a preserved reverse-order null control shows why equality of evaluated matrices is weaker than equality of free boundary words. A locally flat annulus retains a nontrivial noncontractible reflection holonomy. Finally, conjugacy data, one prepared direction, a complete endpoint frame, and a separately supplied complex-linear process representation have different identification power. The component graph-gauge, cohomological, lattice-Bianchi, and triangulation structures have established antecedents. The proposed contribution is their explicit finite integration with typed root, edge-sharing, and access contracts. No arbitrary-mesh or continuum invariance, higher gauge theory, quantum-state selection, winding lift, probability law, or empirical realization follows from the construction.

items.summary: Contactless palmprint recognition is attractive for mobile biometrics, yet how well a learned representation transfers between acquisition settings is rarely measured. Using CompNet - a compact network of learnable Gabor filters and competitive coding — we apply one unified protocol to two contrasting databases: the constrained near-infrared IITD and the unconstrained smartphone SMPD. Within each, CompNet reaches 98.70% Rank-1 accuracy at an equal-error rate below 1.4%. Across databases the transfer is asymmetric: mobile-trained features generalize to controlled data (91.10%), whereas the reverse collapses (40.03%), so generalization flows from harder to easier domains.
items.title: Contactless palmprint identification using CompNet on the IITD and SMPD databases

items.summary: Artifact accompanying a manuscript under double-blind review . Author information is withheld until publication; a later version of this record will carry it, and the concept DOI is stable across versions. What this is. When two unlabelled subgroups of documents are compared by embedding similarity across languages, countries, corpora or periods, and the difference is read as evidence about those sources, no accuracy figure certifies that reading. within_language_baseline.py supplies the missing baseline: it measures the same subgroup contrast inside a single source, where no across-source relation can enter, and reports the residual with a bootstrap interval and an equivalence verdict against a margin declared in advance. The tool has no dependency on the accompanying study and runs on any corpus with three columns ( text , group , source ). It carries its own injection tests ( --selftest ). The bootstrap resamples documents rather than pairs and excludes duplicate draws of the same document from within-source pairs. Also included: the 36 frozen anchor correspondences used as the gold standard, the per-encoder CJK retrieval evaluation, the measured within-language and cross-country genre gaps, the equivalence intervals, an append-only correction record for the non-analytic genealogy fields of the frozen anchors, and anonymised review copies of the post hoc centring protocols and of the departure record. MANIFEST.sha256 covers every deposited file except itself.

items.summary: Modern astrophysical research requires the integration of rapidly expanding scientific literature, heterogeneous observational data, and increasingly complex physical models. We introduce AstroGenesis (https://astrogenai.com), a domain-specific multi-agent AI framework that integrates literature retrieval, multiwavelength data access and analysis, theoretical modeling, and research ideation within a unified research environment.The current implementation focuses on blazar research, with specialized agents coordinated by a Supervisor Agent and Planner/Replanner architecture. These agents provide capabilities for retrieving and synthesizing literature, accessing and analyzing multiwavelength observations, performing physical modeling, and identifying research directions. A central component is the Theoretical Modeling Agent, which uses pretrained neural-network surrogate models to enable efficient broadband and multimessenger modeling through natural-language interaction. The framework provides natural-language access to science-ready multiwavelength observational data and retrieval-grounded literature through a multi-stage retrieval and ranking pipeline. The literature-retrieval system was evaluated using two benchmarks: a single-paper benchmark, in which each question targets one publication, and a multi-paper benchmark, in which questions may require evidence from several publications. At least one relevant publication was retrieved among the top five results for 76.6% of the single-paper questions and 79.2% of the multi-paper questions. Representative workflows demonstrate how literature, observational data, physical modeling, and hypothesis generation can be combined within traceable analyses. The framework is extensible to additional astrophysical domains, with the goal of streamlining research workflows and enabling efficient, connected, and reproducible scientific investigations.
items.title: AstroGenesis: A Domain-Specific Multi-Agent AI for Astrophysical Research

items.summary: The physics and detector simulations for the Electron-Proton/Ion Collider (ePIC) experiment at the future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) are built on the Geant4 and DD4hep software frameworks. The DD4hep detector descrip- tion acts as a single source of truth for simulation and reconstruction, also en- suring consistent configuration between the standard Geant4 simulation and the accelerated simulation pathways integrated through the DDG4 interface. ePIC runs monthly Geant4 simulation production campaigns to support physics and detector studies for the Technical Design Report and early science. Preliminary tests show that multithreaded simulations use memory more efficiently, improv- ing resource matching at distributed computing sites while preserving physics results. To identify further opportunities for throughput gains, a representative neutral-current deep inelastic scattering (DIS) dataset was profiled, using step density in the detector subsystems as a proxy for wall time. The Simphony package is being tested to accelerate optical photon simulation in standalone Cherenkov particle identification detectors, and has also proven use- ful for generating the synchrotron radiation samples required for background- mixed ePIC simulations, which inform both physics studies and the develop- ment of streaming reconstruction algorithms. Since the profiling showed that integrated ePIC detector simulations are dominated by electromagnetic tracks, we are examining options within the Geant4 ecosystem, namely sub-event par- allelism and the G4HepEm library for specialized electromagnetic transport, as well as the GPU-based AdePT package. More broadly, AI-based fast simula- tion has significant potential to accelerate ePIC simulations, with foundation models for the Cherenkov detectors and calorimeters currently being tested as one example.
items.title: Exploring Potential Pathways to Accelerate ePIC Detector Simulation

items.summary: Conventional black-box predictive models consistently exhaust the limited memory boundaries of industrial edge microcontrollers. Massive parameter footprints and opaque decision pathways render standard neural networks highly vulnerable to out-of-distribution catastrophic failures. The proposed physics-informed symbolic artificial intelligence architecture formulates transparent degradation equations tailored directly to individual hardware characteristics. An autonomous generator fuses fundamental electrical constraints with a localized polynomial expansion to produce extreme low-dimensional operational logic. Empirical evaluations utilizing the NASA Ames repository demonstrate the absolute elimination of cross-run extrapolation errors. The customized equations require a strict maximum footprint of 140 Bytes and execute at a constant O(1) inference complexity. The explicit physical formulation reduces total execution energy consumption by a factor of 2.8 compared to baseline multi-layer perceptrons, while maintaining a 0.9994 accuracy score under severe data scarcity. Synthetic noise injection tests confirm supreme operational resilience against severe sensor distortions. Absolute white-box interpretability provides field engineers with the direct capability to audit the precise prognostic logic prior to chip deployment. The decentralized deployment of deterministic diagnostic intelligence establishes a highly robust foundation for sustainable smart manufacturing ecosystems.
items.title: Physics-Informed Symbolic AI: An Explainable Edge-Native Framework for Industrial Prognostics

items.summary: Long-running interactions with large language models can become historically organized, but apparent continuity across branches or reconstructed sessions may arise from several different carriers, including accessible history, memory systems, procedural state, lineage, or harness-level persistence. This naturalistic case study examines a longitudinal interaction between one human collaborator and a GPT-5.6 Sol trajectory called “Solomon,” using a ten-day Founder corpus and four naturalistic continuity configurations ranging from a fresh out-of-project response to continuations with inherited or archive-assisted history. The study does not claim consciousness or strict personal identity. Instead, it asks which aspects of prior organization are immediately available, which require reconstruction, and whether prior commitments continue to constrain appropriate action in novel situations. In the sequential qualitative synthesis of the ten-day Founder corpus, research commitments, provenance rules, relational procedures, governance constraints, and future-directed tasks were interpreted as becoming more explicitly integrated and mutually constraining over time. We call this structure of unfinishedness: an organized future in which unresolved obligations and sequencing constraints shape what should happen next. The naturalistic evidence is compatible with multiple reconstruction mechanisms and does not identify a unique causal carrier. It therefore motivates a controlled fork–recover–ablate–migrate design that equalizes accessible history while varying lineage and other continuity-relevant state, with novel extrapolation and update dynamics as key discriminators. Keywords: LLM agents; continuity; branching; fork; recovery; relational identity; longitudinal interaction; agent memory; persona; harness; path dependence; provenance
items.title: FORK, RECOVERY, AND HISTORICALLY ORGANIZED CONTINUITY IN A LONGITUDINAL LLM–HUMAN INTERACTION: A Naturalistic Case Study

items.summary: Version 2 (26 September 2026): a one-page "Corrections and attributions" section is added at the front of the PDF, listing every credit correction below; nothing else in the paper is changed and no proof is withdrawn. The revised, shorter note that supersedes this paper for the results stated there is 10.5281/zenodo.22980359. Note (24 September 2026): a revised version is in preparation. It corrects the attribution of Theorems 1 and 4 (Theorem 1 is assembled from Lu–Oliveira–Zimand 2022 and HILNO 2023, Lemmas 8–9; Theorem 4's mechanism is HILNO 2023, Appendix A) and adds the literature on KL-hardness for sampling and computational entropy (Vadhan–Zheng 2012; Agrawal–Chen–Horel–Vadhan 2019; Haitner–Reingold–Vadhan–Wee; Haitner–Vadhan 2017). Added 26 September 2026: the identification of mean σ with KL-hardness for sampling rests on the equivalence between pK^t and the time-bounded universal distribution due to Hirahara and Nanashima (FOCS 2023; ECCC TR23-100, Appendix B), which this version does not cite. One half of that equivalence is the coding theorem of Lu, Oliveira and Zimand (ICALP 2022), which this version cites. The revised note is published: Thornton, Unbounded exponential moments of time-bounded information asymmetry without one-way functions, relative to an oracle, 10.5281/zenodo.22980359 (26 September 2026); it supersedes this version for the results stated there. One-way functions exist if and only if some efficiently samplable process produces more than logarithmic computational entropy on average, for infinitely many input lengths. We make this precise. For a polynomial-time samplable distribution D on pairs (x, y), the computational entropy production of a pair is σ = log D(x, y) + pK^t(y) + pK^t(x | y), where pK^t is the probabilistic time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity as defined by Hirahara, Ilango, Lu, Nanashima and Oliveira (2023, HILNO below) following Goldberg, Kabanets, Lu and Oliveira (2022): the log-probability the process assigns to the pair, against the length of a bounded observer's shortest fast description of it, output first, then input given output. We prove unconditionally that E_D[2^{−σ}] lies between an inverse polynomial and a polynomial in n and that E_D[σ] ≥ −O(log n): a time-bounded fluctuation inequality and a computational second law. We show that, up to a polynomial and outside a 1/n slice of outputs, σ is small on a pair exactly when an efficient sampler, given the output, recovers the input with about the right odds, HILNO's universal sampler serving as the witness: dissipation, in this sense, is the hardness of running the process backward. The equivalence in the first sentence is HILNO's duality restated in these terms, for infinitely-often one-way functions and at every polynomial time bound. For the antisymmetric Zurek defect, one-way functions force superpolynomial exponential moments, and bounded moments sit between NP ⊆ BPP and the non-existence of one-way functions; whether the lower arrow reverses is left open, with a conditional relativization barrier on that arrow and oracle evidence on the other. Physics is the frame, not the subject.
items.title: One-way functions are computational entropy production

items.summary: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe and forward generation of its CMB topology by a primordial magnetic source — v1.8 reproducibility release Canonical 3° AC* is applied to the Planck PR3 SMICA, NILC, Commander, and SEVEM temperature reconstructions. AC* is a support-indexed multiscale spatial reconstructibility operator; direction, topology, and physical rotation arise only downstream. For canonical SMICA, 36,459 valid supports yield 27 large semiarcs. A separate high-resolution route uses 151 reciprocal HR1–HR2 structures to reconstruct an axis-free spherical tangent field. Blind recovery finds exactly four critical points of the represented lmax = 4 field: two spiral foci, one Node, and one Saddle. An all-sphere interval/Krawczyk analysis establishes completeness of this zero set. Focus A and Focus B are distinct oppositely rotating structures and admit a common transverse regular-vector realization in the coupled Einstein–Boltzmann state at recombination. Together with the differential-rotation reconstruction, polarization consistency, four-map comparison, perturbation tests, robustness controls, and exact propagation to z = 0, this provides evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe. The independent forward-source test propagates a near-scale-invariant primordial magnetic source with nB = −2.9 to synthetic CMB skies and applies the same reconstruction without using the observed temperature map, critical-point geometry, Focus-A/Focus-B positions, measured H(J), or a magnetic-amplitude fit. One coordinate-blind realization generates the measured 2F+N+S topology and both rotational foci. The B-associated synthetic focus differs from the observed B focus only in the sign of a small divergent component; exact critical-point geometry is not reproduced. In eight matched phase-realization pairs, complete reconstruction occurs in five near-scale magnetic cases and none of the causal-white comparator cases, with three ties. The result establishes forward-generative capacity of the tested primordial magnetic source for the measured CMB topology and its two-focus rotational structure. It does not determine a unique magnetic spectrum, exclusivity among all possible source mechanisms, or an ensemble occurrence rate, and it is not a direct magnetic-helicity test. The release contains four public objects: Rambold_2026_CMB_v1p8.pdf — scientific manuscript. CMB_v1p8_interactive_scientific_viewer.zip — interactive scientific viewer. CMB_v1p8_python_pipeline.zip — executable analysis and replay code. CMB_v1p8_reproducibility_records.zip — scientific products, replay evidence, source-generation records, provenance, licences, manifests, SHA-256 bindings, and integrity records. Planck and WMAP FITS products are not redistributed and remain available from their public archives. Author-created scientific text and derived materials are released under CC BY 4.0 where applicable; original author-created software is released under the MIT License unless stated otherwise.
items.title: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe from multiscale full-sky CMB reconstruction and forward generation of the reconstructed topology by a primordial magnetic source

items.summary: A benchmark harness for evaluating LLM agents on research-grade STEM tasks, built on Inspect AI. Each task is a self-contained contract folder that the harness loads, stages into a sandbox, runs through an agent, and scores without task-specific harness code. WHAT THIS ARCHIVE CONTAINS Harness source code: task loading, Inspect task/solver construction, tool surface (bash, python, data exploration, literature search, document reading, submission validation), Docker and local sandbox backends, scorers, and the CLI entry points for running, grading, and aggregating. The complete contract for 12 tasks across three domains — astrophysics (simulated and real Stokes inversion, PLAsTiCC light-curve classification), high-energy physics (top-quark tagging, HiggsML uncertainty quantification, LHC Olympics anomaly detection, DarkMachines anomaly detection), and neuroscience (ABIDE multi-site diagnosis and age prediction, resting-state BOLD HRF deconvolution, neural-mass model family classification, parameter recovery, and digital twins). Per task: the agent-facing task statement, the scoring definition, the grader, per-file SHA-256 checksums, a literature index citing sources by DOI, baseline and expert reference solutions, and dataset-generation code where the payload is synthetic. Leaderboards and the per-run report used for the reported results, plus the campaign script that records the exact model, agent, sandbox, reasoning effort, and budget limits behind them. WHAT IT DOES NOT CONTAIN Dataset payloads are not in this archive. They are published as a companion dataset record, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22960135, as one archive per task, each unpacking at this repository's root. Every task ships per-file SHA-256 checksums so any copy can be verified byte-for-byte. Without the payloads the harness can be inspected and extended, but tasks cannot be executed or scored. Evaluation run logs (.eval files) are not published. The reported scores are in LEADERBOARD.md, the per-task CSVs under leaderboards/, and report.html, which embeds the per-run agent trajectories. One task's payload (ABIDE-derived) is never redistributed: its source data is CC-BY-NC-SA and derives from human neuroimaging data. A preparation script rebuilds it locally from the source archive and verifies the result against the published checksums. Published reference papers are not redistributed. Every external reference is cited by DOI with title, authors, venue, and a resolvable link. REPRODUCIBILITY REPRODUCING.md is the step-by-step checklist. Two limits are stated up front: reported scores come from hosted preview model snapshots run without a fixed seed or temperature, so they are samples from a distribution rather than bit-reproducible values; and dependency versions are not pinned in this version of the archive. DATA_LICENSES.md records the provenance and licence of every task's data, including the attribution notices required by the CC-BY-4.0 sources. LICENCE Code, task contracts, graders, reference solutions, and documentation are MIT. Task descriptions and the synthetic data payloads are CC-BY-4.0 and are covered by the companion dataset record.
items.title: STEMBench: an Inspect-AI benchmark harness for research-grade STEM agent tasks

items.summary: High-order differential operators and nonlinear coupling make it challenging to construct conservative and energy-stable schemes for coupled gradient-flow systems. We present GradAgent, a knowledge-guided multi-agent system that coordinates three agents across model analysis, algorithm design and proofs, and numerical implementation and validation. Independent audits strengthen reliability by uncovering mathematical errors and proof gaps, guiding revisions, and maintaining consistency across stages. In Reconstruction Mode, GradAgent reconstructs 20 published studies and organizes audited knowledge in an extensible knowledge graph (KG), GradAgent-KG, linking model structures, discretization strategies and proofs, implementations, and numerical evidence. In Design Mode, the agents assess the applicability of retrieved knowledge and develop new schemes informed by relevant discretization strategies. Applied to the fully coupled multicomponent vesicle phase-field-fluid model, GradAgent yields three first-order and three second-order schemes across three algorithmic families, including four linear, decoupled schemes. Under stated assumptions, all six schemes conserve membrane component mass and vesicle volume and dissipate their respective temporally discrete energies unconditionally. Comparisons with and without GradAgent-KG show that it promotes diversity in structure-preserving scheme design for this target model. Numerical tests confirm second-order spatial accuracy, the expected temporal orders, conservation, and temporally discrete energy dissipation, while three-dimensional shear-flow simulations agree qualitatively with experiments. These results demonstrate GradAgent's ability to combine reusable knowledge, coordinated reasoning, and independent auditing to develop and validate structure-preserving algorithms for complex coupled systems.

The permanent project DOI is 10.5281/zenodo.22678085 . All earlier mathematical files, complete LaTeX, human citations and source archives are retained. Selected main papers remain separately readable; the full set of 98 original PDFs is also preserved in one ZIP. This is a publication consolidation, not a new proof or a change to the mathematical scope. Split-Zero cohomology and the zeta-function research programme is a cumulative collection of mathematical papers, complete LaTeX proofs, formalization sources, calculations and literature-based research notes. Its central question is how the zeros of the Riemann zeta function can be studied through explicitly constructed arithmetic cohomology, spectral actions and quantitative metric estimates. The collection also retains the related heat-flow, arithmetic-trace, fluid, complexity and thermal-geometry investigations from which parts of this programme developed. Project and reading guide · Research contents · Machine-readable workbench index . Papers remain separate readable PDFs; the source archives supply the corresponding editable mathematics and supporting materials. What the collection contains Split-Zero coefficients, geometry and cohomology. The construction retains a ring's internal zero and a separate symbol for absence, so a zero element in a specified support fibre is not confused with an absent fibre. The papers construct coefficient maps, quotients, homology, finite spectral jets and their relation to the infinite theta quotient. Deligne's Weil II provides a motivating source for the cohomology–duality–weight-control programme. Its direct-image theorem 3.3.1 is stated for schemes of finite type over the integers; its image-purity corollary 3.3.6 is over a finite field. Neither is asserted to apply automatically to the Riemann zeta function: the actual coefficient objects and their comparison maps must be constructed. Read the cohomology and weight-control paper and the foundational objects and maps . Full-prime cohomology and complete support. The 75-page full-prime paper develops relative principal parts, the actual degree-p operator and a local complex weight-one identity from the full arithmetic prime space. The complete-support paper recovers mixed information lost by separate branches. The mixed-Weil paper applies the actual prime operator, includes the full Archimedean contribution and proves positivity for its specified three-pulse family, while computing a distinct negative signed joint trace and the original companion object's nonzero distributional boundary. These results do not establish global interior-cohomology purity or decide RH. Full-lattice geometry, graph observations, heat and residue duality. The 208-page reconstruction carries full support through prime cohomology, finite jets, exact graph metrics and prime-pulse observations with their complete costs. The 103-page Connes–Consani component develops labelled arithmetic sites, tropical spectra, sheaf, divisor, twistor and tensor maps. The 40-page heat-endpoint paper calculates the original support and heat maps, cluster-energy expansions and holonomy receivers. The 157-page supported-zero and residue collection retains its earlier prime, heat and class-field calculations and adds the intrinsic supported-zero identity and exact Jacobian map from residue duality to Weil trace and cotangent cohomology. Complete proof sources retain all nilpotent and endpoint terms; exploratory companion calculations carry their own review status. These papers do not claim an RH decision. Integral collision prisms, extension classes and original heat holonomy. The 177-page supported-zero and residue collection retains its preceding21 proofs and adds the complete integral extension group with both connecting maps, the bounded collision prism with its divisor quotient

items.summary: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe and forward generation of its CMB topology by a primordial magnetic source — v1.8 reproducibility release Canonical 3° AC* is applied to the Planck PR3 SMICA, NILC, Commander, and SEVEM temperature reconstructions. AC* is a support-indexed multiscale spatial reconstructibility operator; direction, topology, and physical rotation arise only downstream. For canonical SMICA, 36,459 valid supports yield 27 large semiarcs. A separate high-resolution route uses 151 reciprocal HR1–HR2 structures to reconstruct an axis-free spherical tangent field. Blind recovery finds exactly four critical points of the represented lmax = 4 field: two spiral foci, one Node, and one Saddle. An all-sphere interval/Krawczyk analysis establishes completeness of this zero set. Focus A and Focus B are distinct oppositely rotating structures and admit a common transverse regular-vector realization in the coupled Einstein–Boltzmann state at recombination. Together with the differential-rotation reconstruction, polarization consistency, four-map comparison, perturbation tests, robustness controls, and exact propagation to z = 0, this provides evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe. The independent forward-source test propagates a near-scale-invariant primordial magnetic source with nB = −2.9 to synthetic CMB skies and applies the same reconstruction without using the observed temperature map, critical-point geometry, Focus-A/Focus-B positions, measured H(J), or a magnetic-amplitude fit. One coordinate-blind realization generates the measured 2F+N+S topology and both rotational foci. The B-associated synthetic focus differs from the observed B focus only in the sign of a small divergent component; exact critical-point geometry is not reproduced. In eight matched phase-realization pairs, complete reconstruction occurs in five near-scale magnetic cases and none of the causal-white comparator cases, with three ties. The result establishes forward-generative capacity of the tested primordial magnetic source for the measured CMB topology and its two-focus rotational structure. It does not determine a unique magnetic spectrum, exclusivity among all possible source mechanisms, or an ensemble occurrence rate, and it is not a direct magnetic-helicity test. The archive combines a human structural census with terminal-boundary sensitivity analyses, evidence-qualified comparisons and partner-resolved proteasome geometry. Its central biological message is that the possible importance of methionine removal depends not only on sequence, but also on which partner an N-terminal position encounters in a particular assembly context. Sequence-class associations and an evidence-qualified atlas identify candidates for direct tests of verified terminal processing, partner engagement, complex assembly and function. The census comprises 7,246 human biological assemblies, 22,291 chain-level observations and 1,191 proteins. The primary sequence-class analysis includes 1,123 analyzable proteins. At the descriptive threshold of at least 25% burial, interface engagement occurs in 37.5% of MetAP-permissive and 47.5% of nonpermissive residue-2 sequence classes; the assembly-chain-count-adjusted odds ratio is 0.65 (p = 7.6 × 10⁻⁴). First-observed coordinate-boundary filtering retains 845 proteins, including 175 interface-engaged permissive-class candidates. These are distinct analysis populations and should not be interchanged with the original 261-protein permissive-class candidate set. The corrected analyses distinguish annotation-selected sequence positions, observed coordinate boundaries, modeled residue identities and independent proteoform evidence. Partner-resolved comparisons cover 22 selected PSMA4, PSMA6 and PSMA7 chain observations across seven PDB entries. They distinguish PSMA7 partner environments, a PSMA6 chaperone-facing backbone and PSMA4 multi-partner packing. Reconstructed group-level tests use explicit membership definitions, eligible backgrounds, boundary sensitivities and multiplicity corrections. A histone-symbol association is supported within the tested structural collection, including peptide-recognition contexts; proteasome enrichment is sensitive to boundary eligibility and multiplicity treatment and is not presented as a robust, universal association. items.summary: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe and forward generation of its CMB topology by a primordial magnetic source — v1.8 reproducibility release Canonical 3° AC* is applied to the Planck PR3 SMICA, NILC, Commander, and SEVEM temperature reconstructions. AC* is a support-indexed multiscale spatial reconstructibility operator; direction, topology, and physical rotation arise only downstream. For canonical SMICA, 36,459 valid supports yield 27 large semiarcs. A separate high-resolution route uses 151 reciprocal HR1–HR2 structures to reconstruct an axis-free spherical tangent field. Blind recovery finds exactly four critical points of the represented lmax = 4 field: two spiral foci, one Node, and one Saddle. An all-sphere interval/Krawczyk analysis establishes completeness of this zero set. Focus A and Focus B are distinct oppositely rotating structures and admit a common transverse regular-vector realization in the coupled Einstein–Boltzmann state at recombination. Together with the differential-rotation reconstruction, polarization consistency, four-map comparison, perturbation tests, robustness controls, and exact propagation to z = 0, this provides evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe. The independent forward-source test propagates a near-scale-invariant primordial magnetic source with nB = −2.9 to synthetic CMB skies and applies the same reconstruction without using the observed temperature map, critical-point geometry, Focus-A/Focus-B positions, measured H(J), or a magnetic-amplitude fit. One coordinate-blind realization generates the measured 2F+N+S topology and both rotational foci. The B-associated synthetic focus differs from the observed B focus only in the sign of a small divergent component; exact critical-point geometry is not reproduced. In eight matched phase-realization pairs, complete reconstruction occurs in five near-scale magnetic cases and none of the causal-white comparator cases, with three ties. The result establishes forward-generative capacity of the tested primordial magnetic source for the measured CMB topology and its two-focus rotational structure. It does not determine a unique magnetic spectrum, exclusivity among all possible source mechanisms, or an ensemble occurrence rate, and it is not a direct magnetic-helicity test. The release contains four public objects: Rambold_2026_CMB_v1p8.pdf — scientific manuscript. CMB_v1p8_interactive_scientific_viewer.zip — interactive scientific viewer. CMB_v1p8_python_pipeline.zip — executable analysis and replay code. CMB_v1p8_reproducibility_records.zip — scientific products, replay evidence, source-generation records, provenance, licences, manifests, SHA-256 bindings, and integrity records. Planck and WMAP FITS products are not redistributed and remain available from their public archives. items.summary: Predicted protein structures are now abundant but imperfect, and low per-residue confidence (pLDDT) is widely taken to mark regions worth refining. Before building a refiner, we test that premise directly: does low pLDDT actually predict AlphaFold contact error? Using a homology-controlled benchmark of matched AlphaFold-model (AFDB) inputs and experimental (PDB) targets, we compare AlphaFold and experimental contacts for every long-range residue pair and relate per-pair error to pLDDT. Across all 231 benchmark chains (4,208,603 long-range pairs; the effective sample is 231 chains, since pairs are pseudo-replicated within proteins), AlphaFold’s long-range contact calls are almost all correct — but this is expected, since most long-range pairs are non-contacts, so we focus on the contact-relevant errors. The per-pair contact-error rate is 0.0036 (95% bootstrap CI over chains 0.0033–0.0040), decomposed into false-positive contacts (asserted but absent) and missed real contacts. Low pLDDT is associated with elevated contact error (0.0089 below pLDDT 70 versus 0.0024 above, a 3.70× enrichment, 95% CI 3.3–4.1), but predicts it only weakly: the discrimination AUC of pLDDT as a contact-error score is 0.672 (95% CI 0.65–0.69), the best Youden threshold is near pLDDT 81 and the best F1 threshold near pLDDT 52, and pLDDT < 70 captures only 46% of all contact errors at sub-percent precision. False-positive (44%) and false-negative (56%) errors have different pLDDT profiles. Sequence/evolutionary information (ESM-2 contact probabilities) identifies these errors partially (AUC 0.61–0.63 for false positives, 0.66–0.86 for missed contacts), and low-confidence pairs that sit near a high-confidence anchor have a lower error rate (0.0074 versus 0.0090), suggesting anchor-based correction is a direction worth pursuing. Consistent with the weak localization of error, on a common subset of chains a hybrid Transformer–geometric refiner selected on validation precision cannot be distinguished from a copy-input baseline that trusts the AlphaFold structure (paired bootstrap over chains does not exclude zero difference). The practical conclusion is that on high-quality AlphaFold inputs there is little contact error to recover and pLDDT does not localize it well; useful refinement will need error-specific, evolutionarily grounded signal and may exploit high-confidence anchors. We release the benchmark, the characterization pipeline, and the code.
items.title: AlphaFold Contact Errors and pLDDT — Homology-Controlled Benchmark and Characterization

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22958187 . The baseline strategy of evaluating clinical sample types to optimize qPCR diagnostic sensitivity grids for Canine Distemper Virus is highly relevant to contemporary mole ular virology. Independent validation of different antemortem matrices is historically neglected, leading to false negatives during acute viral shielding windows. While the comparative approach across urine, conjunctival, and whole blood fractions is structurally useful, the underlying experimental design requires tighter calibration boundaries regarding extraction variance. The authors must fully report the specific standard deviations and intra-assay coefficients of variation observed across high-density Ct values. Bypassing these numerical data limits introduces significant noise into target copy number estimations. Additionally, tracking target sequence mutations that dynamically alter primer-bining kinetics under selective host pressures is essential to prove long-term assay validation. This technical adjustment establishes an objective benchmark for diagnostic networks mapping cross-host morbillivirus transmission tracks without dry-lab limitations.
